items.explanation: 日 is a picture of the sun and means sun or day. 日曜日 uses both readings: にち at the start and び (ひ with dakuten) at the end. It is also the 日 in 日本 (にほん, Japan).
items.mnemonic: A window with the sun shining through it.
items.culture_note: 日本 means origin of the sun, which is why Japan is called the land of the rising sun.

items.explanation: 月 means moon and month. It is read ゲツ in 月曜日 (Monday) and ガツ in month names such as 一月 (いちがつ, January). The moon itself is つき.
items.mnemonic: A crescent moon drawn as a tall box with two lines inside.

items.explanation: A picture of flames rising from a fire. It is read カ in 火曜日 (かようび, Tuesday); fire itself is ひ.
items.mnemonic: A person waving both arms next to a campfire.

items.explanation: A picture of water flowing in a stream with splashes on each side. It is read スイ in 水曜日 (すいようび, Wednesday); water itself is みず.
items.mnemonic: A river in the middle, with drops splashing out on both sides.

items.explanation: A picture of a tree: trunk, branches, and roots. It is read モク in 木曜日 (もくようび, Thursday); a tree itself is き.
items.mnemonic: A tree with arms spread out and roots going down.

items.explanation: 金 means gold, metal and money. It is read キン in 金曜日 (きんようび, Friday); money is おかね, written お金.
items.mnemonic: A roof over a pile of gold nuggets.

items.explanation: A sprout coming out of the ground. It is read ド in 土曜日 (どようび, Saturday); soil itself is つち.
items.mnemonic: A plus sign planted on the ground: something growing from the earth.
items.culture_note: The days of the week are named after the sun, the moon and five planets: 火星 Mars, 水星 Mercury, 木星 Jupiter, 金星 Venus and 土星 Saturn. It is the same scheme as in English, where Saturday is Saturn's day.
